A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PQN research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and can be matched despite substantial theoretical revisions and reorganisation.

before.justification: v2 reports original experiments on Baird’s counterexample, Atari, Craftax, MinAtar and several multi-agent environments, including ablations and appendix results.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and adds results on parallelism in MinAtar and stronger regularisation in Baird’s counterexample.

M1.justification: Equation (9) changes the regularised TD update from penalising only final-layer weights to also penalising the hidden-layer matrix, with an explicit eta > 1 condition. The practical lambda-return, minibatch and multi-epoch procedure already appeared in v2’s Algorithm 2; its appearance in v3’s Algorithm 1 is largely expanded documentation and relocation.

E1.justification: The evaluated environments and tasks are retained, including MinAtar, DeepSea, classic control, Atari, Craftax, SMAX, Overcooked, Hanabi and Baird’s counterexample. The new MinAtar parallelism sweep changes configurations within existing task coverage.

E2.justification: Corresponding benchmark comparisons retain the same baseline algorithms, including PPO, DDQN, prioritised DDQN, Rainbow, CleanRL-DQN and the existing MARL baselines. The additional higher-L2 Baird curve varies regularisation strength within an existing ablation rather than introducing a distinct baseline algorithm.

E3.justification: The new MinAtar sweep varies parallel environments from 1 to 512, adjusting minibatches and epochs to control gradient steps and batch size, with learning-rate adjustments where necessary. Table 3 revises reported PPO/PQN update counts at 200M frames from 700k to 780k and Rainbow’s from 50M to 12.5M; these reporting revisions do not establish that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v3 adds a systematic test of the central parallelism design choice: aggregate and per-game sample-efficiency and time-efficiency analyses across four MinAtar tasks and nine environment counts (Figures 6e and 10–12). It also adds a stronger-L2 setting to the Baird ablation. These substantially extend evidence about when parallelism and regularisation help.

E5.justification: Both versions report 10 seeds generally and 3 seeds for ALE, with existing IQM summaries and shaded variability plots retained. The added experiments do not introduce a different uncertainty-reporting practice or an explicit increase in repeated runs.

E6.justification: New MinAtar curves show learning with one environment and improved aggregate sample and time efficiency with greater parallelism; Baird gains a higher-L2 result. Section 5.2 also reduces the reported gradient-update comparison from over 50 times to over 16 times. Main benchmark scores, including Tables 3 and 9, remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 3 and Appendix B substantially revise the mathematical foundation. v3 replaces the earlier Lipschitz activation specification with C2 pre/post-normalisation activations and bounded second derivatives, revises width-dependent bounds and the regularisation conditions, and uses the symmetric Jacobian part in Theorem 1’s eigenvalue argument. It also corrects LayerNorm derivatives and adds derivations of the stability decomposition and recursive lambda-returns.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion narrow the practical claim from eliminating replay buffers to eliminating large replay buffers. v3 explicitly distinguishes the buffer-free theoretical result from practical PQN’s small trajectory buffer. The central claims of simplicity, competitive performance and substantial training-speed advantages remain.

C2.justification: v3 explicitly states that convergence to a TD fixed point does not imply zero value-function error and clarifies PQN’s focus on simulator-based parallel-world problems. It interprets the new parallelism results as showing that multiple environments improve efficiency without being essential for learning. The earlier limitation concerning the absence of prioritised replay is removed.

D1.justification: v3 replaces the anonymous repository reference with a stated public GitHub repository and explicitly describes the I*T trajectory buffer and minibatch sampling. Hardware, optimiser and hyperparameter Tables 4–8 are retained. However, Algorithm 1 line 14 introduces a positive squared-error gradient step where v2’s Algorithm 2 used descent, creating a reproducibility inconsistency.

R1.justification: v3 adds Boyd and Vandenberghe, Kolter, and Liu et al. (2020), while removing Lee et al. (2019). It explicitly positions the practical lambda-return procedure as a parallelised version of Daley and Amato’s approach, already cited in v2, and narrows the claimed normalisation analysis to LayerNorm when discussing CrossQ.

P1.justification: Sections 3–4 and the proof appendix receive substantial explanatory rewriting, including geometric intuition, proof roadmaps and a reorganised algorithm description. The practical algorithm moves from Appendix C into the main text, duplicate regularisation-related-work material is consolidated, and subsequent appendices are reorganised.

P2.justification: v3 adds the geometric stability diagram and MinAtar parallelism plots, expands the main result and ablation figures, and revises Figure 1’s labels and caption. Baird’s plot gains a curve and revised vertical scaling and is also displayed in the main text. Other benchmark graphics and table structures are largely retained.

improvement.justification: v3 improves precision through revised regularisation conditions and mathematical corrections, more accurate buffer and update-count claims, and controlled evidence about parallelism. These strengthen explanation and support without changing the main benchmark conclusions. The gains are tempered by the newly incorrect gradient sign in Algorithm 1, which weakens reproducibility and prevents an unqualified substantial improvement.
